Sourcing a reconditioned unit that includes a refurbished water pump, updated coolant crossover pipes, and a verified oil cooler provides the best long-term value. failures.title: Land Rover 306PS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Cooling System Leaks (Water Pump & Crossover Pipes)
items.whatHappens: The 306PS utilizes several plastic and composite cooling components, including the water pump housing and coolant crossover pipes. Over time, heat cycling causes these materials to degrade, leading to slow coolant loss, sweet-smelling steam from the engine bay, and potential overheating if ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the water pump and crossover pipes is a standard preventative repair. However, if the leak has been ignored and the engine has overheated, cylinder head warpage may occur, necessitating a full Land Rover 306PS engine replacement.

items.title: Oil Cooler Issues & Particulate Filter Regeneration
items.whatHappens: Occasional oil cooler seal degradation can lead to internal or external leaks. Additionally, on L405 hosts, oil dilution can occur as a byproduct of frequent, incomplete particulate filter (GPF/DPF) regeneration cycles, particularly in vehicles subjected to short, urban journeys.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the oil cooler is a straightforward repair if caught early. To mitigate oil dilution, owners are advised to ensure regular sustained high-speed driving to allow regeneration cycles to complete, or to adhere to strict, shortened oil change intervals.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 306PS is generally considered a robust and reliable unit within the modern Land Rover lineup. Its failure rate is notably lower than older supercharged variants, provided the cooling system is monitored and full JLR service history is maintained .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 306PS
variants.intro: As a Specific page type with no distinct sub-codes listed in the inventory, this section focuses on accurate identification and avoiding common, costly misidentifications. The 306PS engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the cylinder block and is also recorded on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Owners frequently confuse the 306PS with its predecessor, the AJ126, or the diesel variant, the 306DT. While the AJ126 is also a 3.0-litre supercharged V6, it is a Jaguar-sourced architecture with different mounting points, engine management calibration, and cooling system layouts. The 306DT is a twin-turbo diesel V6 with an entirely different internal architecture and emissions system. Fitting an AJ126 or 306DT wiring harness, ECU, or ancillary components to a 306PS host will result in a non-running vehicle and significant wasted expenditure.

relatives.description: The - the Jaguar-sourced 3.0-litre supercharged V6 that the 306PS replaced in Land Rover's lineup, offering similar power outputs but with a different mounting layout and cooling system architecture.

The (P400) - the modern mild-hybrid 3.0-litre inline-six that is gradually superseding the V6 architecture in newer Land Rover models, offering improved efficiency, electrification, and a fundamentally different internal layout.
The - the 3.0-litre twin-turbo diesel V6 that shares the same L405 and L494 chassis applications but features a completely different internal architecture, block design, and emissions system.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 306PS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover 306PS engine for sale can be a viable option for rolling restorations, provided the seller can confirm the cooling system has been recently serviced and there is no history of overheating or oil dilution. Without this history, you risk inheriting age-related plastic cooling component degradation. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most modern Land Rover owners, a reconditioned 306PS is the optimal choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine’s known weaknesses by fitting a refurbished water pump, updated coolant crossover pipes, and a verified oil cooler, delivering near-new reliability for future high-performance driving. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for low-mileage, high-spec L405 or L494 projects where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for line-boring the main bearings, balancing the rotating assembly, and ensuring the engine matches the pristine condition of the flagship chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your replacement through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with modern Land Rover wiring and supercharger systems, backed by a nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit availability.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Modern Range Rover L405 and Range Rover Sport L494 models typically hold values between £30,000 and £80,000, depending on mileage, specification, and condition . Because a fully reconditioned Land Rover 306PS engine replacement is well within this value band, replacement is generally a financially sound decision, provided the vehicle's overall body condition and service history are sound.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Land Rover 306PS engine?
items.answer: The most documented failures on the 306PS relate to the cooling system, specifically water pump housing and plastic coolant crossover pipe degradation. Over time, heat cycling causes these components to crack, leading to slow coolant loss and potential overheating. Occasional oil cooler seal issues and oil dilution from incomplete particulate filter regeneration cycles are also noted on higher-mileage examples.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 306PS engine?
items.answer: The 306PS engine was fitted to the Land Rover Range Rover (L405) and Range Rover Sport (L494) between 2014 and 2020. It served as the premium supercharged petrol option, often badged as P380. It replaced the older Jaguar-sourced AJ126 architecture. It was designed to offer refined power delivery and seamless integration with modern vehicle electronics.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 306PS engine?
items.answer: For a modern Land Rover, a reconditioned 306PS is strongly recommended over a used unit. Used engines frequently inherit the same age-related plastic cooling component degradation that prompted the original removal. A proper reconditioned build proactively replaces the water pump, updates the coolant crossover pipes, and verifies the oil cooler integrity. Reconditioned units also include comprehensive compression and pressure testing to guarantee reliability.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 306PS engine?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document under the "Engine Number" field or by locating the code stamped on the cylinder block. The 306PS is a 3.0-litre supercharged V6, easily distinguished from the diesel 306DT by its supercharger assembly and lack of diesel emissions equipment. It is also distinct from the older AJ126, which features different mounting points and engine management calibration. Fitting an AJ126 or 306DT wiring harness to a 306PS host will result in a non-running vehicle.
